drivers: HRV is stable (recent_avg = baseline_avg = 60.6 ms; latest = 65.0 ms)
Sleep is chronically insufficient (recent_avg = 4.7 h, 7/14 nights <7h)
Training readiness avg_7d is low (34.4), though latest improved to 53
ACWR = 0.8 — within optimal band but trending toward detraining if sustained
Body Battery is up +9.6 vs baseline (+17.4%), suggesting compensatory recovery capacity
readiness.guidance: The athlete is holding steady but not fully recovered — prioritize sleep extension and avoid intensity increases until sleep debt improves.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows meaningful pace improvement and increased high-zone work, but at the cost of reduced cadence and rising aerobic TE — a sign of accumulating fatigue masked by higher-intensity focus.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite fewer runs and less volume, average pace improved by 20 sec/km — driven by a sharp increase in Z4/Z5 work (19% → 7% last month, but Z4 alone jumped from 15% to 19% and Z5 from 1% to 7%), indicating intentional intensity shift rather than organic fitness gain.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 61.0 km, 9.4 km across ~4 sessions are needed in 13 days — but with chronic sleep debt (4.7 h avg) and declining cadence/efficiency, chasing volume would compound fatigue. Prioritizing recovery over mileage is the correct call.

insights.title: Chronic sleep deficit correlates with reduced running economy stability
insights.body: Sleep average is 4.7 h (7/14 nights <7h); during this period, Running Economy latest value (262.2) is 8.2 ml/kg/km above rolling median (253.9), and vertical ratio rose to 10.93% — both signs of compromised neuromuscular efficiency linked to sleep loss.

insights.title: ACWR of 0.8 coincides with improved aerobic decoupling — but only recently
insights.body: Latest aerobic decoupling is 0.84% (well under 5%), yet median recent decoupling is 6.66%; the improvement follows a drop in acute load (191 vs chronic 227) and lower recent TRIMP (+30.6% vs baseline but down from June’s 645), suggesting the current 'optimal' ACWR is enabling better endurance integrity — but it’s fragile without sleep recovery.

insights.title: Z4/Z5 work increased sharply but efficiency per beat declined in those zones
insights.body: Z4 % rose from 15% to 19%, Z5 from 1% to 7%, yet efficiency in Z5 dropped to 0.6742 m/beat — the lowest across all zones and 11% below Z2 (0.7891), indicating diminishing return on high-intensity effort without commensurate aerobic foundation or recovery.

insights.title: Cadence drop and stride length variability reflect fatigue despite stable VO2max
insights.body: Cadence fell from 151 spm (Jun) to 147 spm (Jul), and stride length varied widely across recent runs (70.4–89.8 cm), while VO2max held at 39.0 — suggesting neuromuscular fatigue rather than cardiovascular limitation, likely amplified by sub-5h sleep.

recommendations.action: Two Zone 1 runs (HR <125 bpm, 45–55 min) on Monday and Thursday — no pace target, focus on cadence ≥145 spm and relaxed breathing
recommendations.reason: Restores autonomic balance without adding load; supports HRV stability and counters recent cadence decline

recommendations.action: One 30-min non-running active recovery session (e.g., cycling or swimming at RPE ≤3) on Wednesday with emphasis on 8+ hours sleep that night
recommendations.reason: Breaks sleep debt cycle while maintaining circulation; Body Battery is elevated (+9.6), making this a strategic window to consolidate recovery

recommendations.action: Skip all Z4/Z5 efforts next week; replace planned interval session with 6 × 2-min Z3 strides (HR 150–158 bpm) embedded in 8 km easy run, full 2-min walk recovery between
recommendations.reason: Maintains neuromuscular stimulus without decoupling risk (latest decoupling was 0.84% only in a Z3-run); avoids further efficiency decay in high zones where m/beat is already lowest

risk_flags.risk: Cumulative sleep debt impairing movement efficiency and injury resilience
risk_flags.evidence: 4.7 h avg sleep, 7/14 nights <7h; vertical oscillation increased to 8.5 cm (7.6–8.5 range), ground contact time variability up to 22 ms (300–322 ms), stride length variance >19 cm
risk_flags.action: Prioritize sleep extension to ≥6.5 h for 5+ nights before reintroducing Z4 work

risk_flags.risk: Efficiency decay in high-intensity zones may reinforce poor pacing habits
risk_flags.evidence: Z5 efficiency (0.6742 m/beat) is 11% lower than Z2; best 1k effort (365s) occurred during June’s higher-sleep, lower-Z5 month — not during current high-Z5 phase
risk_flags.action: De-emphasize race-pace efforts until Z5 efficiency improves to ≥0.70 m/beat and sleep stabilizes ≥6 h

weekly_focus.description: Stabilize sleep and autonomic tone first, then rebuild efficient movement patterns at sub-threshold intensities — not to chase speed, but to restore the biomechanical foundation that makes faster running sustainable.
